source_text:
Ἄξια μὲν
σκότους πράγ-ματα ἐννοούμενον ἔσωθεν· διὰ δὲ τῶν ἔξωθεν μερῶν, φωτὸς εἶναι
δοκοῦντα προφέρον ῥήματα· λύκοι γάρ εἰσιν ὡς ἀληθῶς, προβάτων περιβεβλημένοι
δοράς· οἱ τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος μόνον πλύνοντες, καὶ οὐκ
εἰδότες, ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ τὸ ἔσωθεν τούτων καθαρισθῇ, οὐδὲ τὸ ἔξωθεν καθαρὸν δύναται
thought_title: Hypocrites speak light but think darkness
orientation: Gregory is describing the hypocrite whose evil eye darkens the whole body, now detailing how such a person thinks dark deeds inwardly while speaking words that seem full of light.
pass_a_gloss: Worthy indeed of darkness are the deeds he devises within; but through the outward parts he brings forth words that seem to be of light; for they are truly wolves, having put on sheep's clothing; they wash only the outside of the cup and the dish, and do not know that unless the inside of these is cleansed, neither can the outside become clean.

choices.english: Worthy indeed of darkness are the deeds
choices.why: The μὲν sets up the contrast with the outward words; 'indeed' preserves the particle's force without overtranslating.
rejected: The deeds are worthy of darkness

choices.why: The participle is masculine singular, referring back to the hypocrite; 'devises' captures the active plotting sense of ἐννοέω.

choices.english: that seem to be of light
choices.why: δοκοῦντα marks the appearance as deceptive; 'seem to be of light' preserves the genitive φωτὸς as a quality.
προφέρω means to utter or bring out; 'brings forth' keeps the outward direction implied by the contrast with ἔσωθεν.
The glossary mandates 'sheep's clothing' for προβάτων δοραί; περιβεβλημένοι is a perfect participle, hence 'having put on.'

choices.term: οὐδὲ τὸ ἔξωθεν καθαρὸν δύναται γενέσθαι
choices.english: neither can the outside become clean
choices.why: The negative οὐδὲ with δύναται preserves the logical impossibility; 'become clean' renders γενέσθαι καθαρὸν as a change of state.
rejected: the outside cannot be made clean
nor is the outside able to be clean

bible_refs.note: οἱ τὸ ἔξωθεν τοῦ ποτηρίου καὶ τῆς παροψίδος μόνον πλύνοντες
λύκοι γάρ εἰσιν ὡς ἀληθῶς, προβάτων περιβεβλημένοι δοράς

pass_b_english: They devise deeds worthy of darkness within, yet through their outward parts they bring forth words that seem to be full of light. For they are truly wolves who have put on sheep's clothing (Matthew 7:15). They wash only the outside of the cup and dish (Matthew 23:25), not knowing that unless the inside is cleansed, the outside cannot become clean.

last_rejected.why: Source alludes to Matthew 7:15, not a direct quote; parenthetical citation is misleading.
last_rejected.ruling: Standard scholarly practice: parentheticals identify allusions, not claim direct quotes.

problems.quote: They devise deeds worthy of darkness within
problems.why: Unclear if 'they' refers to hypocrites generally or specific group; no antecedent since last noun was 'evil eye'.

edits.old: They devise deeds worthy of darkness within
edits.new: These hypocrites devise deeds worthy of darkness within

fixed: Clarified 'They' to 'These hypocrites' to provide an antecedent for the pronoun.
